hazard: Missed opportunity for appropriate VTE risk management
theme: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

reports.title: Francoise Snape
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: No VTE assessment was ever made of Mrs Snape. The explanation given oy was that staff were too busy to complete the form and that because she had had a stroke heparin could not be given and therefore the Paperwork was unnecessary
concerns.hazard: lack of VTE assessment for stroke patient

concerns.quote: NICE guidelines regarding the use of mechanical anti DVT devices instead of heparin in high risk cases was not considered
absence of a formally completed VTE assessment and lack of knowledge of NICE guidelines amounted to a lost opportunity to make informed decisions for the care of Mrs Snape
concerns.hazard: missed opportunity for appropriate VTE risk management

reports.title: Mathew Bailey: Prevention of future deaths report

concerns.quote: charts monitoring his intake and output of fluids should have been started and maintained, but were not. Nurses should do this as a matter of course for any patient with a urinary or kidney infection, and the doctors who reviewed him regularly during his 5 day admission should also have picked up on the fact that his fluids were not being monitored
concerns.hazard: lack of fluid monitoring for kidney infection patients

concerns.quote: a venous thromboembolism ( VTE ) assessment was carried out, which identified that the deceased had an identified risk of suffering a VTE event and prescribed compression stockings to mitigate that risk. Both the nurses and doctors looking after the deceased should have picked up on this, but did not, with the result that the deceased was without VTE prophylaxis for the duration of his admission
concerns.hazard: absence of VTE prophylaxis despite identified risk

links.explanation: Both reports concern failures to provide appropriate venous thromboembolism prophylaxis despite awareness of risk. The earlier case involved no assessment and ignorance of guidelines; the later case involved an assessment that was not acted upon.
